title: Does the EU AML Regulation (AMLR) apply to online marketplaces? | Customer Due Diligence Guide
summary: When the EU AMLR applies to an online marketplace, how it reaches marketplaces via payment providers and which seller checks the DSA requires.
body_markdown:
*When the EU AMLR covers a marketplace, how it reaches marketplaces through their payment providers, and which identity checks the Digital Services Act already requires.*


An online marketplace is not an obliged entity under the EU Anti-Money Laundering Regulation (AMLR), which applies from 10 July 2027, merely because it is a marketplace: the list of obliged entities in Article 3 does not include online platforms as such. The AMLR applies to a marketplace when it carries out an activity on that list, for example when it is authorised as a payment or electronic money institution, trades in precious metals and stones or in high-value goods as a regular or principal professional activity, or trades or acts as an intermediary in the trade of cultural goods worth EUR 10,000 or more. Separately, the Digital Services Act already requires business-to-consumer marketplaces, other than micro and small enterprises, to identify their traders.


*Written by Aleksander Wasiak (Compliance Officer) and Ivan Mikić (International Sales Director), Authologic.*
